subject: Post-demo: OrbitAI streaming rehearsal & traffic/setup
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <ogrant@orbitai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: streaming SLOs & customer-led rehearsal

Hi Marcus / Grace / Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo today — very helpful. A quick recap from OrbitAI's side and what we want to run for the customer-led rehearsal:

- SLOs we care about: 95th pct streaming chunk latency <= 200ms, end-to-end first-token < 450ms for short responses, and sustained per-connection throughput of roughly 1–2KB/s for high-token streams.
- Target throughput: ramp to 400 req/s, steady-state 300–400 req/s.
- Concurrency: ~120–180 simultaneous streaming clients (we'll target 150).
- Duration: 30 minute steady-state window after ramp.
- Tooling: we'll run a k6-based harness (attached: orbit_k6_profile_v3.js) from our cloud account (AWS us-west-2).

What we need from Redwood to proceed:
1) A short-lived test API key and test account (scoped to our rehearsal).
2) IP allowlist entries for our egress ranges (we will provide our CIDRs).
3) Confirmation on how streaming is measured on your side (per-chunk vs per-response), and whether batching is automatically applied for streaming requests.
4) Recommended ramp pattern to avoid priming artifacts.

Proposed windows (PDT):
- Thu Aug 11, 09:00–11:00 (primary)
- Thu Aug 11, 22:00–00:00 (fallback for APAC overlap)

I'll attach our k6 script (orbit_k6_profile_v3.js). Aaron Patel (copied) will run the harness from our test project. Please let us know if you can provide the test creds and IP allowlist template today so we can add entries from our side.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Grant
Head of Platform Engineering, OrbitAI
ogrant@orbitai.com

Attachments: orbit_k6_profile_v3.js, profile_readme.md
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <ogrant@orbitai.com>, Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@orbitai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming SLOs & customer-led rehearsal

Hi Olivia / Aaron — great to see alignment, and thanks for the clear targets. Below is a concise plan and what we'll provide from Redwood for the rehearsal.

What Redwood will provide (pre-test):
- Test API key (scoped) and a test account: redwood-test-orbit-XXXX (see attached redwood-test-account.txt for placeholder creds).
- IP allowlist template (attached ip_allowlist_template.txt). Our public-facing egress ranges you can add: 34.120.0.0/16, 52.24.128.0/18, and 18.196.0.0/15. If you plan to run k6 from additional cloud regions, send those CIDRs and we can add them temporarily.
- A short runbook and checklist (attached runbook-orbit-rehearsal.pdf) with prewarming, expected metrics, and post-test artifacts.

Streaming measurement notes:
- Redwood measures streaming latency at the per-chunk emission level for profiling, and also reports first-token latency (for E2E). For your SLOs: we will report 50/95/99 for chunk latency and first-token.
- For customer-led k6 runs, we recommend disabling automatic server-side batching (if your script supports toggling) so you exercise low-latency streaming. Redwood can also run a mirrored test with batching enabled if you want a comparison.

Recommended k6 ramp pattern (our suggestion to avoid cache warm-up spikes):
1) 0–5min: ramp from 0 to 40 rps
2) 5–15min: ramp to target 400 rps
3) 15–45min: steady-state 300–400 rps (30 min steady state)
4) 45–50min: ramp down gracefully

Streaming-specific settings: target 150 concurrent streaming clients, set read/chunk size to match your client (we recommend 256–512 bytes chunk).

Proposed final window: Thu Aug 11, 09:00–10:30 PDT (we can shorten to 90 minutes). Please confirm final window and your egress CIDRs and we'll provision the test account and apply allowlist entries.

Attachments: redwood-test-account.txt (API key stub), ip_allowlist_template.txt, runbook-orbit-rehearsal.pdf, redwood-k6-adapter.sh (helper script)

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming rehearsal & traffic/setup (internal)

Marcus / Vivek — quick internal checklist before we hand off to customer ops: 
- Vivek: can you prewarm 2x dedicated streaming pools (same model family) for Aug 11 08:30 PDT and keep them in warm state until 11:00? We'll need KV cache warm and a reserved slot for heavy tail.
- Please enable enhanced tracing for that window (token-level sampling 1/1000) so we can capture any regressions quickly.
- Ops contact: I'll loop in Sam R. (not on this thread) to watch infra metrics.

I'll prepare a short Slack playbook and join the call during the test.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Customer Reliability
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <ogrant@orbitai.com>, Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@orbitai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming SLOs & customer-led rehearsal — final confirmation

Olivia / Aaron — confirmed on our side for Thu Aug 11 09:00–10:30 PDT. Final checklist below and attachments included. Please reply ACK when you've added the listed CIDRs into your outbound allowlist so we can finalize provisioning.

Final checklist (Redwood + OrbitAI):
- [Redwood] Provision test API key and bind to orbit test account (attached redwood-test-account.txt) — DONE, key issued but inactive until allowlist confirmed.
- [OrbitAI] Add Redwood CIDRs to your egress allowlist: 34.120.0.0/16, 52.24.128.0/18, 18.196.0.0/15 — ACTION: OrbitAI to confirm.
- [Both] Agree on k6 ramp and concurrency (150 concurrent streams, 30 min steady-state).
- [Redwood] Prewarm streaming pools at 08:30 PDT and enable enhanced tracing.
- [OrbitAI] Run orbit_k6_profile_v3.js with the redwood-k6-adapter.sh helper; send test run logs to rerun@redwoodinference.com.
- [Both] After test: share traces and request/response samples for 95/99 percentile analysis.

Attachments: runbook-orbit-rehearsal.pdf (final runbook), redwood-test-account.txt (API key stub), ip_allowlist_template.txt

Looking forward — reply ACK when the CIDRs are added and we'll flip the key active.

Best,
Marcus
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
